mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses equity discount rates, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds without requiring additional conditions.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical inverse correlation between FEDFUNDS and equity returns
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 9.0% signals severe economic distress, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days. This threshold is based on historical market reactions to high unemployment.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical market downturns during unemployment spikes
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 9.0% (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above their 3-month moving averages indicates robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days. The interaction effect is non-additive and requires both series to be rising.
evidence_refs: fact:Consumer demand leading to equity market gains
failure_condition: The interaction of HOUST and RSAFS above their 3-month MAs does not produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases (i.e., positive returns in < 40% of triggered instances).

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 220) erodes corporate profit margins and increases risk aversion, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. This relationship is observed during high inflation regimes.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical equity market declines during high inflation
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative when CPIAUCSL > 220 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Higher housing starts (HOUST) consistently indicate improving economic conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days. This relationship holds without requiring additional conditions.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical correlation between HOUST and equity returns
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly positive when HOUST is above its 3-month moving average (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90.0 signals a manufacturing contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days. This threshold is based on historical manufacturing downturns.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical market reactions to manufacturing contractions
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO < 90.0 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 220) creates a 'stagflation' environment, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. The interaction effect is non-additive and requires both conditions to be met.
evidence_refs: fact:Stagflation periods leading to equity market declines
failure_condition: The interaction of FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 220 does not produce negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases (i.e., negative returns in < 40% of triggered instances).

mechanism_narrative: Low quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 < 13000) signals a slowing economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days. This threshold is based on historical GDP growth rates during economic slowdowns.
evidence_refs: fact:Historical market downturns during GDP slowdowns
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 < 13000.0 (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.05.
